# Learn HAX

> Tutorials, reference, and onboarding for the HAX ecosystem.

HAXcms is a file-based CMS: authored pages and metadata are stored as portable files, not locked into a database-only workflow.
The canonical site structure is `site.json`, represented in JSON Outline Schema (`id`, `parent`, `order`, `slug`, `location`, and `metadata`).
Use HAX CLI and ecosystem tooling to maintain human-authored content while keeping machine-readable outputs synchronized.
Managed files (feeds, search indexes, manifests, and this `llms.txt`) are generated artifacts and should be rebuilt by tooling.

## Core resources
- [site.json](https://learn.hax.cloud/site.json): Canonical site manifest and navigation tree in JSON Outline Schema format.
- [llms.txt](https://learn.hax.cloud/llms.txt): LLM-oriented guide to this site and its machine-readable resources.
- [llms-full.txt](https://learn.hax.cloud/llms-full.txt): The whole site as one markdown document, in outline order.
- [Whole site as HTML](https://learn.hax.cloud/x/api/v1/site/export/html): Every page in one HTML document.
- [AGENTS.md](https://learn.hax.cloud/AGENTS.md): Instructions for AI agents working on this site's files.

- [Fill in the Blanks](https://learn.hax.cloud/pages/item-146c5613-144a-4b57-800f-73e4affe28d5/index.md): This question type allows the user to complete a sentance by answering in context of other written material.
- [Mark the Words](https://learn.hax.cloud/pages/item-dab9887d-4ca6-4e89-b8ae-b1ae0e7566c9/index.md): Mark the Words allows you to write a sentence and have the user select individual words as solutions to the question.
- [Matching / Drag and Drop](https://learn.hax.cloud/pages/item-90093686-d1c7-4464-8656-0f407e82e193/index.md): Matching question, often called a drag and drop, allows for setting drop targets to possible matching answers.
- [Multiple Choice](https://learn.hax.cloud/pages/item-d003549b-8e72-4887-9e63-ebc8392625fe/index.md): When reading content or processing a lecture, it's a good idea to stop and ask the user questions about what they experienced.
- [Short Answer Question](https://learn.hax.cloud/pages/item-838af7af-7e6f-45de-8f75-8728d0fc5643/index.md): Short answer supports multiple possible answers and is best utilized with single words for accuracy in user entry.
- [Sorting Question](https://learn.hax.cloud/pages/item-6995c339-78b2-44ef-82a7-9f93c8ac2a8f/index.md): Sorting questions can be used to make users place items in the correct order.
- [Tagging Question](https://learn.hax.cloud/pages/item-bb895134-c091-41fb-abb0-0a37b1c17fe7/index.md): Tagging questions allow for a drag and drop or click to select method of answering.
- [True / False Question](https://learn.hax.cloud/pages/item-ef38f789-2cd8-4400-8e25-e34f4b48ff24/index.md): A simple question type that allows you to supply the question but the user only can pick between true and false.
- [Self Check](https://learn.hax.cloud/pages/item-00f0e62b-01d4-4202-add8-7e8490122049/index.md): Sometimes after a video or reading a section of content we have a simple question that we want the user to ask themselves to reflect.
- [Stop Note](https://learn.hax.cloud/pages/item-08a260e1-c5be-4f4e-ae8e-b6083916bb90/index.md): There might be times when we've given out a lot of information to our users all at once, or perhaps there's a critical piece of detail we want to reemphasize before we move on.
- [Table](https://learn.hax.cloud/pages/item-5efd455d-d2b8-4127-a4c4-f7c7dfc4d153/index.md): The effective sharing and display of large data tables helped build the web as we know it.
- [Timeline](https://learn.hax.cloud/pages/item-e16de22c-5a24-4bc4-890f-0a3054ecdae9/index.md): Events happen in a sequence, but sometimes it's hard to convey the same meaning in pure written form.
